The present appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, assailing the award dated 30.11.2016 passed by the 5th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 85/2015, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality and are not under challenge in the present appeal.

compensation to the tune of Rs.50,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization was awarded.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4467 2 MA-244-2017 4.
Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that the compensation awarded is inadequate.

It is contended that the appellants, being real brothers of the deceased, were fully dependent upon him, and the Claims Tribunal committed an error in not considering their Raghwendra vs Shri Pal on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106153689/
1 dependency.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is, therefore, prayed that the compensation amount be enhanced and a just and reasonable amount be awarded.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for any enhancement.
He supports the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
Upon appreciation of the evidence, particularly the testimony of Raghvendra Sharma, it is evident that the claimants were not dependent upon the deceased.

Therefore, the Claims Tribunal has rightly held that the claimants are not entitled to compensation on the basis of dependency in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 .

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, the claimants are entitled to compensation under the conventional heads, namely loss of estate and funeral expenses, to the extent of Rs.30,000/-.
8.
Accordingly, the present appeal is allowed in part .

The compensation is enhanced by Rs.30,000/-
(Rupees Thirty Thousand Only), which shall be payable to the appellants in addition to the amount already NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4467 3 MA-244-2017 awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal, from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain undisturbed.
The appeal stands disposed of in the above terms.
